Bernadette M. Wilson

Registered Republican candidate for Governor / Lieutenant Governor, Alaska · Open seat

Business owner (Denali Disposal); conservative activist

Bernadette M. Wilson is a Republican business owner from Anchorage. She was born in Kenai and owns Denali Disposal. She announced her campaign for governor on May 13, 2025, and has never held elected office. She advanced from the August 18, 2026 nonpartisan top-four primary to the November 3 general election, and her running mate for lieutenant governor is Mike Shower.

Where Wilson stands

Permanent Fund Dividend
Supports paying the full statutory (formula) dividend, about $3,800 this year. She says lawmakers should 'follow the formula' and was the only debate candidate to back a formula dividend.
Permanent Fund
Says the dividend formula creates an obligation to Alaskans that should be repaid, even if that means breaking the current spending limit on the Permanent Fund.
State services and budget
Proposes an audit of state government to find efficiencies and tasks that can be automated, plus a yearly 'state of the budget address.'
State workforce
Has said she would shrink the state workforce to deal with the budget. She argues Alaska has one of the highest numbers of government employees per capita.
Resource development
Supports moving energy and mining projects forward in partnership with the Trump administration and argues her Democratic opponent would block them.
Education funding
In her official election statement, she says Alaska's education ranks near the bottom and pledges that 'our children will attend the best schools.'
Abortion
Endorsed by Alaska Right to Life Action. The group said she was the only candidate for governor who met with it on its priorities, including ending state funding for abortion.
